question.text: Which pricing model is described as 'relatively simple and fast' and does not rely on calculation by iteration?

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook describes Black-Scholes as relatively simple and fast and non-iterative, while the Binomial model is described as lengthy and time-consuming because it builds a tree of possible prices through iteration. The Trap: Binomial uses iteration. Monte Carlo uses simulation. Black-Scholes provides a closed-form approach, which is why it is characterised as quick and direct. Note: Stop at the source-supported contrast: Black-Scholes versus Binomial in terms of iteration and speed.
